circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has been the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's earlier establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Melbourne's Albert Park Circuit winds around a lakeside urban park and hosts the Australian Grand Prix, Formula One's traditional season-opener. The track also accommodates the Supercars Championship and various support series, holding the highest FIA classification for permanent circuits.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally opened as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually from 1970 to 1987 before being reconfigured and rebranded as the A1-Ring. Following further modifications, the venue resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track situated in Azerbaijan's capital near Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before being renamed the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Located in Bahrain and spanning 5. 412 kilometers, this FIA Grade 1 circuit has been hosting motorsport events since its 2004 opening, including the region's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix. The venue accommodates various racing categories such as drag racing, endurance competitions, and single-seater series, while also featuring alternative track configurations for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, situated in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations. With FIA Grade 1 status and spectator capacity exceeding 140,000, the venue serves as a comprehensive test of driver and car performance across multiple racing disciplines.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian circuit sprawling across 7. 004 kilometres near Stavelot in Wallonia has served as the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix venue since 1925, participating in the sport's inaugural season in 1950. It has maintained an almost continuous presence on the championship calendar from 1985 onwards, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km track that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has also accommodated various international motorsport competitions including sportscar championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, the Shanghai International Circuit serves as the primary venue for the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The facility has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024, establishing itself as a significant racing destination in China.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English racing venue hosted the inaugural world championship grand prix in 1950 and has served as the primary home of Britain's Formula One race since 1987, after decades of rotation with other circuits. The track also features prominently on the international motorcycle racing calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km permanent facility located near Budapest, Hungary, hosting the annual Hungarian Grand Prix since 1986 when it became the first Formula One race held in Eastern Europe. Built in remarkably quick time of just eight months starting from late 1985, the circuit was constructed outside the city near a main highway after plans for a street-racing venue in Budapest's largest park were rejected by authorities.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Italy's Monza Circuit, established in 1922 near Milan, ranks among the world's earliest purpose-built racing venues and remains mainland Europe's oldest. The 5. 793 km track earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" because of its extended straights and fast corners, hosting the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949 as a cornerstone fixture of the Formula One championship.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland with a 155,000-spectator capacity. The track is renowned as a premier destination for Formula One racing and hosts one of the championship's most iconic Grand Prix events.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its collection of major casinos and hotels. The track weaves past several iconic Las Vegas landmarks, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two Mexican racing brothers who died in motorsport accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The circuit has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, with its current continuous tenure beginning in 2015 on a revised layout, now officially called the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Florida, measuring 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the championship calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, threading around the principality's harbor. Though officially named for Monaco, the circuit is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of its layout traverses that particular neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the Zandvoort circuit is a 4. 259 km track that hosted Formula One's Dutch Grand Prix following its return to the calendar in 2021. The venue's partnership with the sport concluded after the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motor racing venue situated north of Doha, featuring a 5. 419-kilometer track with a notably long main straight spanning 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian motorsport venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track features supporting facilities including a karting circuit dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since its debut in 2021, while also accommodating Formula E racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue in Singapore that winds through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts, centered around the Marina Bay waterfront area.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a diverse mix of long straights and varied corner types that make it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The track holds FIA Grade 1 status and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside other major motorsport events including NASCAR and MotoGP. The venue has established itself as a premier racing destination by regularly staging multiple international racing series across different disciplines.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he secured back-to-back world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship and claiming two Le Mans 24-hour victories with Toyota, making him the sole driver to have captured both a Formula One world title and a World Endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli is an Italian Formula One driver competing for Mercedes who has claimed eight Grand Prix victories following his entry into the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British racing driver Oliver Bearman currently races for Haas in Formula One competition. He competes at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races for Audi in Formula One after establishing himself as a talented competitor in the sport's top tier.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that has yielded ten Grand Prix victories. He achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during 2019 and 2020 while competing for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian racing driver, holds a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One while primarily competing in European endurance racing for Nielsen Racing. Between 2024 and 2025, he participated in seven Formula One Grand Prix events.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver with French and Algerian heritage competing for France, currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple racing records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi and has also competed extensively in endurance motorsport, where he achieved victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently races in Formula One as a member of the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monégasque driver Charles Leclerc competes for Ferrari in Formula One, where he finished second in the 2022 championship standings. Across his nine seasons in the sport, he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in endurance racing with BMW's WRT team and part-time in NASCAR, driving the No. 91 Chevrolet for Trackhouse Racing. He previously held an F1 seat across two separate periods, racing from 2014 to 2020 and returning for the 2022 to 2024 seasons.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Over his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One for the Haas team.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac and brings considerable experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian racing driver currently competing in Formula One with McLaren. Across four seasons in the sport, he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has claimed four Grand Prix victories over the course of his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to international sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in the IMSA series.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese racing driver currently holding a reserve position across Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. After five seasons as a full-time competitor from 2021 to 2025, he transitioned to a backup role for the 2026 season.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024, establishing himself as one of Formula One's most successful competitors with 71 race victories accumulated over 12 seasons.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, a Chinese racing driver, currently holds a reserve position with Cadillac in Formula One. He competed as a full-time driver in the championship from 2022 through 2024, representing a historic milestone as the only driver from China to have raced in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based Alpine team has competed in Formula One since 2021, when Renault rebranded its works operation to showcase its Alpine sports car division. Operating under various sponsorship arrangements, the team maintained Renault's factory status until the manufacturer's withdrawal from the sport following the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through multiple incarnations as a British manufacturer, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury manufacturer Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad, famously nicknamed "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, has established itself as a dominant force throughout the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, debuting on the grid in 2016 with support from Toyota's racing division. Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal position in 2024, taking over from Guenther Steiner who had led the organization since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, competed in Formula One from 1993 until 2025, becoming one of the sport's longest-running independent constructors before being acquired by Audi. Prior to its F1 entry, the team earned acclaim in endurance motorsport, including victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours alongside Mercedes-Benz. Audi's 2024 purchase of the team and its operations provided the technical foundation for the manufacturer's return to Formula One.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, which is fully owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One continuously since 1954 as both a manufacturer and team owner. The current squad, officially Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, operates from Brackley under a German licence and became a three-way partnership in January 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The team is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two constructors under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second racing operation in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024, based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned constructors alongside Red Bull Racing, the team operates as part of the energy drink company's dual-team structure in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has competed in Formula One since 2005 as one of two squads controlled by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the squad from its inception through 2024, after which Laurent Mekies assumed the team principal role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in the 2026 season.
